mergedParams.userDescription: Text 'locked' to the camera's motion, perfectly stable in frame. typo kinetics for titles/captions/other text..

output.title: Camera-Locked Typography with Stable Kinetic Text Effects

prompts.prompt: Create a typokinetics preset where text appears perfectly locked to the camera frame as if it's mounted on a steadicam rig. From a video editing perspective, imagine the text as a fixed overlay that maintains perfect stability even when the underlying video has camera movement - like those stabilized GoPro shots where the horizon stays level. The text should feel like it's floating in 3D space at a fixed distance from the viewer, completely immune to any camera shake or movement. Use a BaseLayout container with 'fixed inset-0 pointer-events-none' to create an overlay that spans the entire viewport. Inside, position multiple TextAtom components at different depths using translateZ transforms to create parallax-free text layers. Apply a subtle drop shadow and slight blur to background text elements to enhance depth perception. The key animation should be a gentle breathing effect (scale 1.0 to 1.02) that makes the text feel alive while maintaining its locked position. For captions, implement word-by-word reveals where each word fades in with opacity 0→1 over 300ms but maintains its exact screen position throughout.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='fixed inset-0 z-50 pointer-events-none' containing nested BaseLayouts for each text layer. Use TextAtom components with transform: perspective(1000px) translateZ(0) for GPU acceleration. Apply will-change: transform to all text elements. Implement a custom effect using generic keyframe animations with ranges for scale (1.0→1.02→1.0) over 4s loops with ease-in-out timing. For word reveals, use caption data's words array and apply opacity effects with staggered delays based on word.relativeStart. Use 'font-bold text-white' for primary text, 'font-medium text-white/80' for secondary. Add drop-shadow-2xl for depth. Set fitDurationTo='children' to match caption duration. Consider using an internal effect preset for the breathing animation that can be reused across multiple text elements.

prompts.prompt: Design a documentary-style lower third typokinetic preset where text tracks perfectly with the frame like professional broadcast graphics. Think of how CNN or BBC overlays stay rock-solid during handheld footage - the text should have that same professional stability. Create a two-tier layout: main title and subtitle, both locked to specific screen coordinates. The text should slide in from off-screen with a motion blur effect, then lock into position with a subtle bounce that settles into perfect stillness. Add a animated underline that extends from 0 to 100% width beneath the main title. The entire composition should feel like it's rendered in post-production, completely independent of camera movement. For enhanced visual interest, add a subtle RGB glitch effect that triggers every 3-4 seconds, splitting the color channels momentarily before snapping back.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Use BaseLayout with containerProps.className='absolute bottom-20 left-10 w-auto'. Create two TextAtom children: title with 'text-4xl font-bold tracking-tight' and subtitle with 'text-xl font-light mt-2 text-gray-300'. Implement slide-in using translateX(-100vw)→translateX(0) over 600ms with cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1). Add motion blur via filter: blur(8px)→blur(0). Create underline with ShapeAtom using 'h-1 bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-500 to-cyan-400' and scaleX animation 0→1. For RGB glitch, use three overlapping TextAtoms with mix-blend-mode and translateX offsets, triggered via waveform effects if audio present. Set will-change: transform, filter on animated elements. Use fitDurationTo='parent' and implement effects via generic keyframe animations with specific timing ranges.

prompts.prompt: Build a parallax-free floating caption system where text behaves like UI elements in a video game HUD - completely stable and unaffected by camera motion. Imagine Destiny or Apex Legends' on-screen text that stays pixel-perfect while the game world moves dynamically. Create a grid-based layout system where captions can appear in any quadrant of the screen, with smooth transitions between positions. Each text block should materialize with a digital 'data stream' effect - characters appearing sequentially with a typewriter animation combined with a subtle scanline overlay. Add a holographic shimmer using animated gradients. The text should pulse gently with an energy field effect, as if powered by an internal light source.
prompts.technicalSpecs: Structure: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='grid grid-cols-3 grid-rows-3 fixed inset-0 gap-4 p-8'. Use caption data to dynamically position TextAtoms in grid cells via 'col-start-X row-start-Y'. Implement typewriter effect by rendering each character as a span with staggered opacity animations based on index * 50ms delays. Add scanline overlay using ::before pseudo-element with repeating-linear-gradient and translateY animation. Create holographic effect with background: linear-gradient animated via background-position. Use 'font-mono text-cyan-400' for tech aesthetic. Apply text-shadow: 0 0 20px for glow. Pulse effect via generic keyframe animation on opacity (0.9→1→0.9) and filter: brightness(100%→120%→100%). Consider using internal effect presets for typewriter and pulse animations. Set fitDurationTo='captions' for automatic duration matching.

prompts.prompt: Develop a cinematic title card preset where text is locked to frame like opening credits in a Fincher film - meticulous, precise, and completely stable. The text should fade in through a film grain texture, as if being exposed on actual film stock. Create a sophisticated composition with primary title text centered, surrounded by smaller supporting text elements (director, producer, etc.) arranged in a classic film poster layout. Each text element should have a subtle film gate wobble (±1-2 pixels) to simulate projection while maintaining overall stability. Add a vintage film burn effect that occasionally flares across the text. The entire preset should evoke the feeling of text that was carefully composited in post, with that distinctive locked-to-frame stability of professional title sequences.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full bg-black'. Primary TextAtom with 'absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 text-6xl font-serif tracking-widest text-amber-50'. Supporting text using multiple TextAtoms positioned with 'absolute top-[X%] left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2'. Film grain via overlay div with noise texture and mix-blend-mode: overlay, opacity: 0.3. Gate wobble using generic keyframe animation with translateX/Y ±2px on 3s loop with ease-in-out. Film burn effect using ShapeAtom with radial-gradient, animated via opacity and scale transforms. Add filter: sepia(0.2) contrast(1.1) to all text. Use fitDurationTo='input' for manual duration control. Consider sub-preset for individual credit blocks that can be reused with different text content.

prompts.prompt: Create a sports broadcast typokinetic preset where statistics and player names stay locked on screen like ESPN or Sky Sports graphics. Think of those real-time stats overlays during live games - perfectly stable regardless of camera pans or zooms. Design a modular system with animated stat bars, percentage circles, and data tables that slide in from screen edges. Text should appear with a competitive energy - sharp, bold, and dynamic. Include number counting animations for statistics, progress bar fills for percentages, and color-coded performance indicators. Add subtle particle effects behind important numbers to emphasize updates. The overall feel should be high-energy but professionally locked to the viewing frame.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='fixed inset-0 pointer-events-none'. Create stat modules using nested BaseLayouts with 'absolute' positioning and Tailwind classes like 'bg-gradient-to-r from-red-600/90 to-red-800/90 backdrop-blur-sm rounded-lg p-4'. Use TextAtom for labels with 'font-bold text-white uppercase tracking-wide text-sm'. For counting animations, use generic keyframe effects to animate textContent numbers. Progress bars via ShapeAtom with scaleX animations. Implement slide-ins using translateX with spring easing. Add particle system using multiple small ShapeAtoms with 'rounded-full bg-yellow-400' animated via translateY and opacity. Use CSS containment (contain: layout style paint) for performance. Apply will-change sparingly only during animations. Consider audio-reactive waveform effects for emphasis moments if audio track available.

prompts.prompt: Design a minimalist Swiss-style typokinetic preset where text maintains absolute geometric precision locked to the frame. Channel the Helvetica documentary aesthetic - clean, purposeful, and mathematically positioned. Text should appear through precise rectangular masks that reveal letters with surgical accuracy. Create a grid system based on the golden ratio where text elements align to invisible guidelines. Implement a sophisticated reveal where text doesn't just fade in, but is unveiled through animated crop rectangles that expand from single points. Add subtle baseline shifts and kerning animations that fine-tune the typography while maintaining the locked position. The entire composition should feel like it's been meticulously designed in a grid system and rendered with absolute precision.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full' containing an invisible grid system using CSS custom properties --golden-ratio: 1.618. Position TextAtoms using calculated values like 'absolute top-[calc(50%/var(--golden-ratio))]'. Use clip-path: polygon() for precise masking with animated coordinates. Implement 'font-sans text-black' with specific font-weight variations (300, 400, 700). Create reveal animations using clipPath transitions from inset(50%) to inset(0). Add letter-spacing animations via generic keyframe effects (0.05em→0.15em→0.1em). Use transform-origin to control rotation points for any subtle rotations. Baseline shifts via translateY micro-animations (±0.5em). Consider using sub-presets for individual text blocks that follow the grid system. Set fitDurationTo='scene' for scene-based timing.

prompts.prompt: Build a retro-futuristic typokinetic preset inspired by 80s motion graphics where text is locked to frame like old analog video titles. Think Blade Runner's Voight-Kampff test UI or TRON's digital readouts - text that's burned into the video signal itself. Create a CRT-style display with text that has subtle RGB color separation, scanlines, and phosphor glow. Implement a data corruption effect where text occasionally glitches but immediately re-locks to position. Add VHS tracking lines that pass through without affecting text position. Include a retro computer terminal typing effect with block cursor. The preset should feel like text overlaid on analog video through a vision mixer, maintaining that characteristic locked stability of hardware-based titling.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full bg-black overflow-hidden'. Create CRT effect container with 'before:absolute before:inset-0 before:bg-gradient-to-b before:from-transparent before:via-green-500/5 before:to-transparent before:animate-scan'. TextAtom components with 'font-mono text-green-400' and multiple text-shadows for glow: '0 0 5px #0f0, 0 0 10px #0f0, 0 0 15px #0f0'. RGB separation using three identical TextAtoms with 'absolute' positioning, slight translateX offsets, and mix-blend-mode: screen. Implement glitch via rapid position changes using generic keyframe animations with random translateX/Y values returning to 0. VHS lines using animated divs with 'h-px bg-white/20'. Terminal cursor via ShapeAtom with opacity blink animation. Add filter: contrast(1.2) brightness(1.1) to enhance CRT look. Use will-change: filter for glitch moments only.

prompts.prompt: Create a motion-tracked UI preset where text behaves like AR interface elements perfectly locked to the viewer's perspective. Imagine Iron Man's HUD or Black Mirror's augmented reality - text that exists in a layer between the viewer and the content. Design circular targeting reticles with data readouts, distance measurements, and environmental annotations. Text should materialize with a holographic assembly animation - building up from wireframe to solid. Include reactive elements that pulse when 'scanning' or 'analyzing'. Add subtle chromatic aberration at the edges of text elements to sell the AR projection effect. The composition should feel like advanced military or sci-fi targeting software with rock-solid frame lock.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='fixed inset-0 perspective-1000' for 3D space. Create reticle using SVG circle in ShapeAtom with stroke-dasharray animation for rotation effect. TextAtoms positioned around reticle using transform: rotate(Xdeg) translateX(200px) rotate(-Xdeg) for circular placement. Holographic assembly via opacity and strokeWidth animations on text paths. Use 'font-light text-cyan-300 uppercase tracking-widest text-xs' for data readouts. Chromatic aberration using three text layers with 'mix-blend-mode: screen' and slight color channel offsets. Pulse effects via waveform effects if audio available, otherwise generic keyframe animation on filter: brightness(). Add backdrop-filter: blur(1px) to text containers for depth. Implement 'scanning' animation using linear gradient animated via background-position. Consider internal effect presets for reusable pulse and scan animations.

prompts.prompt: Design a documentary interview typokinetic preset where speaker identification and context remain locked while maintaining elegant editorial pacing. Think of Ken Burns documentaries or true crime series - text that provides essential information without disrupting the visual narrative. Create a sophisticated lower third system with speaker name, title, and contextual information that reveals through subtle material design elevation. Text should lift off the background with realistic shadow progression, then settle into a locked position. Add a timeline indicator that shows speaking duration. Include gentle emphasis animations for keywords extracted from caption data. The entire system should feel editorial and journalistic while maintaining absolute frame stability.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='absolute bottom-0 left-0 right-0 p-8'. Create elevated container with 'bg-white/95 backdrop-blur-md rounded-t-2xl shadow-2xl p-6 transform transition-all duration-700'. Primary TextAtom with 'text-3xl font-serif text-gray-900 mb-2'. Secondary info with 'text-lg text-gray-600'. Implement elevation animation using translateY(100%)→translateY(0) combined with shadow progression (shadow-md→shadow-xl→shadow-2xl). Timeline indicator using ShapeAtom with scaleX animation based on duration. For keyword emphasis, parse caption.words for keyword=true and apply subtle scale(1.05) and font-weight increase. Add ease-out timing for natural motion. Use fitDurationTo='captions' to sync with speech. Consider sub-preset for timeline component that can calculate and display progress. Include will-change: transform during initial animation only, then remove for performance.

prompts.prompt: Build a live event typokinetic preset that mimics professional broadcast graphics packages - think Olympics coverage or award shows. Text should be locked to frame with the precision of expensive broadcast equipment. Create a dynamic system with animated backgrounds, gradient wipes, and particle celebrations that all respect the text's locked position. Design modular components: main title bar, scrolling ticker, countdown timer, and score display. Each module should animate in with broadcast-quality motion design - smooth, professional, and perfectly timed. Add metallic shine effects that sweep across text periodically. Include confetti or firework particle systems for celebration moments. The preset should convey the excitement of live events while maintaining the rock-solid stability expected from professional broadcast graphics.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps.className='relative w-full h-full'. Main title bar using 'absolute top-0 left-0 right-0 h-24 bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-600 via-purple-600 to-pink-600'. TextAtom for title with 'text-5xl font-black text-white drop-shadow-lg'. Scrolling ticker using overflow-hidden container with translateX animation looping from 100% to -100%. Countdown timer with individual TextAtoms per digit using 'tabular-nums' for stability. Metallic shine via animated linear-gradient overlay with background-position animation. Particle system using multiple ShapeAtoms with physics-based animations (translateY for gravity, translateX for wind, rotate for spin). Use transform: translateZ(0) for GPU acceleration on all animated elements. Implement staggered animations using delay calculated from index. Consider audio-reactive waveform effects for celebration triggers. Use internal effect presets for shine and particle animations. Set fitDurationTo='input' for precise broadcast timing control.
